label: Couchbase Server 7.1
type: the Couchbase Server release that lifted the single-root-certificate limit (multiple CAs per cluster) and consequently made no-downtime CA rotation possible; also the release from which node addition must use a secure connection.
evidence: Prior to Couchbase Server Version 7.1, a Couchbase-Server cluster could maintain at most _one_ root certificate.
Note that in Couchbase Server Version 7.1 and later, multiple root certificates can be uploaded.
This restriction is lifted in version 7.1: therefore, root and intermediate certificates _can_ now be used.
note: Promoted because it is the pivot the whole certificate-management story turns on: three separate security pages date their central capability to it.
